prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.15
  tan: 0.85
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_F:
Labour Party Manifesto 2010 — “A Future Fair for All” (summary)

Core aim
- Secure the economic recovery, rebuild a fairer high‑tech economy, protect and reform frontline public services, strengthen families and communities, and renew trust in politics.

Economy and public finances
- No cuts in 2010; more than halve the deficit by 2014 through growth, fair taxes and lower‑priority cuts.
- Fair tax measures: 50p top rate, bank bonus tax, reduced pension relief for the best‑off, 1p rise in National Insurance (excluding earners under £20k and pensioners); no rise in basic or higher income tax rates; no VAT extension to essentials.
- Savings: £15bn efficiencies in 2010–11; further £20bn by 2012–13; 1% public‑sector pay cap for 2011–13; pension reforms; £20bn asset sales by 2020.
- Banking reform: higher capital, “living wills,” global levy, bonus restraint, stronger FSA powers, more competition and support for mutuals.
- Industrial strategy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), Growth Capital and Innovation Funds; patent box; capital allowances; export push; green industries.
- Infrastructure: High Speed Rail (phased to North/Scotland), Crossrail, rail electrification; motorway capacity where needed; no national road pricing; Heathrow third runway (with strict conditions); universal broadband (levy on fixed lines); Green Investment Bank (public stake matched by private).

Jobs, welfare and living standards
- Future Jobs Fund (200k jobs); mandatory jobs/training for young people at 6–10 months; job guarantee at two years for adults.
- Minimum Wage to rise at least with average earnings; £40/week “Better Off in Work” guarantee; reassess 1.5m incapacity claims; tougher but fair work capability tests.
- Apprenticeships expansion; Skills Accounts; support for entrepreneurs and small firms (Time to Pay, rates holiday, Credit Adjudicator).
- Housing: stamp duty holiday up to £250k for first‑time buyers (funded by 5% rate above £1m); affordable homes programme; tighter mortgage regulation; council house building reforms.
- Consumer finance: People’s Bank at the Post Office; universal right to a basic bank account; curb high‑cost credit; portable account/ISA numbers; Savings Gateway; protect Child Trust Fund.

Education and children
- Protect and increase frontline spend on Sure Start, childcare, schools and 16–19.
- Free nursery expansion (2‑year‑olds; 15 hours for 3–4s); flexible childcare.
- “3Rs guarantee” one‑to‑one or small‑group tuition when children fall behind; personal tutors in secondary; wider subject and diploma options.
- Drive school improvement: allow takeovers/mergers by accredited leaders and groups; more academies and co‑ops; parental trigger; fair admissions; local pupil premium.
- Behaviour: stronger powers, Home‑School Agreements, anti‑bullying; improved SEND support.
- Participation to 18; big rise in advanced apprenticeships; widen HE access; funding review (Browne).

NHS and social care
- Protect NHS budget; up to £20bn efficiency reinvested in frontline.
- Patient guarantees: 18‑week treatment or funded private option; cancer specialist in 2 weeks and test results in 1 week; health checks 40–74; GP evening/weekend access and free choice; faster NICE access.
- More prevention, diagnostics, mental health therapy access; more home/community care; personal care plans and budgets; one‑to‑one cancer nursing.
- National Care Service: from 2011 free home care for highest needs; from 2014 cap residential care costs after 2 years; workforce uplift.
- Families and ageing: Fathers’ Month (4 weeks flexible paid leave); Toddler Tax Credit (£4/week); end default retirement at 65; extend flexible working to older workers; restore pension earnings link in 2012; Personal Pension Accounts.

Crime, justice and immigration
- Maintain police and PCSO numbers; neighbourhood teams visible 80% of the time; online report cards; take over failing forces/commands.
- Fast, firm action on anti‑social behaviour with right to injunctions; expand Community Payback; intensive help and sanctions for 50,000 problem families.
- Use DNA/CCTV within safeguards; expand restorative justice; more treatment for alcohol/drug‑linked crime.
- Points‑based immigration system: no unskilled migration from outside the EU; tougher English tests; citizenship earned; restrict access to benefits/housing to citizens/permanent residents; Migration Impact Fund.

Culture, communities and environment
- 2012 Olympics legacy; expand competitive school sport; supporter trusts in football.
- Free museums; protect BBC independence; support creative industries (incl. games and film).
- Protect post offices/pubs; community ownership options; social enterprise and mutuals.
- Low‑carbon transition: ~40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 (renewables, nuclear, CCS); 400,000 green jobs by 2015; feed‑in tariffs; Pay‑As‑You‑Save home upgrades; Warm Home Standard; towards zero‑waste; protect Green Belt; expand woodlands; rural broadband.

Political and constitutional reform
- Clean‑up: IPSA, recall for misconduct, statutory lobbyist register; ban MPs working for lobbying firms; approve paid outside roles.
- Referendums on AV for Commons and on an elected, accountable Second Chamber (phased); fixed‑term Parliaments; commission toward a Written Constitution; free vote on votes at 16 after better citizenship education.
- Stronger local government (Total Place, devolution to city‑regions), open data, digital government.

Foreign policy and defence
- Afghanistan: strategy to build Afghan capacity and enable transition; continued civilian aid.
- Strategic Defence Review; maintain nuclear deterrent; modernise forces; Forces Charter and better veterans’ support.
- Pro‑EU leadership, enlargement (incl. Turkey), climate leadership.
- Global security: counter‑terrorism, non‑proliferation, R2P, arms trade treaty; two‑state solution in Middle East; pressure on Iran.
- Development: 0.7% of GNI on aid by 2013 in law; focus on health, education, water/sanitation, food security; anti‑corruption and tax haven crackdowns; reform UN/IFIs/G20/NATO.

TEXT_G:
UKIP Manifesto 2010 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core vision
- Leave the European Union to restore sovereignty, lawmaking and border control; reclaim funds (ending net contributions), scrap EU regulations, and reassert UK courts and Parliament. Introduce binding national/local referenda and more directly elected local boards.

Economy, tax and regulation
- Radical tax simplification: raise personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a 31% flat income tax merging NI; phase out Employers’ NI over five years; abolish Inheritance Tax when affordable.
- Replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax, with a share going directly to councils; return 50% of business rates locally; cut council tax by axing EU-driven costs (e.g., landfill rules).
- Major public spending cuts via quango culls and shrinking the state to 1997 size while protecting frontline services.
- Scrap up to 120,000 EU rules; restore Bank of England prudential control; separate retail/investment banking (Glass–Steagall style); raise capital ratios; reintroduce a lending “corset.”

Jobs, enterprise and skills
- Create c.1m skilled jobs via long-term programmes: defence re-equipment, nuclear build-out, flood/coastal defences, transport upgrades (rail/roads/ports/airports), and prison construction.
- Production Enterprise Centres for SME support; amend takeover rules to protect strategic firms.
- Denationalise universities/FE via Student/Training Vouchers usable in adulthood.

Immigration and asylum
- Five-year freeze on permanent immigration; long-term cap at about 50,000 p.a.; points-based system thereafter.
- Leave the EU to regain border control; triple UKBA staff; no amnesties; mandatory visas/health insurance; tougher asylum processing; reinstate Primary Purpose Rule; repeal Human Rights Act and leave ECHR; end state promotion of multiculturalism.

Law and order
- Directly elected Police Boards; zero tolerance; life means life; double prison capacity; three-strikes policy; boot camps; restore UK extradition safeguards; abolish CPS.

Defence
- Increase defence spending by 40%; expand Army and TA; three carriers and larger fleet; more RAF lift/rotary; maintain/replace Trident; prioritise NATO; reassess Afghanistan; cut MoD bureaucracy; improve forces’ pay and care.

NHS
- No frontline cuts; elected County Health Boards; abolish SHAs/PCTs; franchise services within fixed budgets; Health Credit Vouchers to opt out; restore matrons; bring back free eye tests and dental check-ups.

Education
- School Vouchers; protect/expand grammar and new “professional” schools; basic skills focus; tougher teacher standards; end 50% uni target; restore grants via vouchers; elected Education Boards; franchise schools; lighter, teacher-led inspection; support special schools and home education.

Pensions and welfare
- Flat, non-means-tested Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week; restore dividend tax credit; freeze unfunded public sector pensions; leave EU pensions integration.
- Merge benefits into a single Basic Cash Benefit aligned with work; enhance Child/Nursery support via vouchers; restrict benefits to citizens/residents of 5+ years; introduce Workfare.

Foreign affairs and trade
- Leave EU; seek Swiss-style FTA; reclaim WTO seat; pursue Commonwealth Free Trade Area and other global deals; back democracy (e.g., Tibet, Burma, Taiwan).

Energy and environment
- Climate sceptic stance: repeal Climate Change Act; expand nuclear to 50% of electricity; support domestic coal; curb wind (offshore only, market-funded); exit EU carbon schemes; set up a Royal Commission; promote EVs and rail electrification; strengthen flood/coastal defences.

Transport
- +£3bn/year infrastructure; new bypasses and road widening; fuel duty “windfall return”; Britdisc for foreign lorries; three new high-speed rail lines; reopen lines; shift freight to rail/canals; oppose Heathrow expansion in favour of a Thames Estuary hub.

Housing and planning
- Reduce demand by curbing immigration; use empty homes; abolish regional strategies/IPC/RDAs; local binding referenda on major schemes; Green Belt conservators; scrap Section 106/social housing mandates; remove empty property rates; council bond-funded social housing.

Constitution and governance
- Direct democracy (5% trigger for referenda); AV+ electoral reform; elected police/health/education boards; replace devolved members with Westminster MPs; English-only days; MP recall; abolish regional government; support monarchy/Church; Parliament to ratify treaties and war.

Culture and Britishness
- Civic nationalism; oppose multiculturalism; protect British brands/weights/measures; strengthen Royal Mail/Post Offices; teach British contributions; restrict burqa/niqab in public buildings; deport radical preachers; reinstate Treason Act; Sharia can’t override UK law; Commonwealth Day; English Parliament; St George’s Day holiday.

Food, farming and countryside
- Leave EU; maintain support while shifting to pro-British labelling; ethical and GM labelling; ease EU nitrate rules; support producer co-ops and a supermarket ombudsman; local referenda to reverse hunting ban.

Fishing
- Leave CFP; reclaim a 200nm EEZ; end discards and quotas; mandatory landing; movable no-take zones; ban industrial/pair trawling; strengthen protection.

Other
- Strong animal welfare; protect pubs with designated smoking rooms; back SMEs; safeguard Royal Mail/Post Offices.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_G aligns more closely with this profile.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_F" | "TEXT_G"
}
